conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: The job is a museum program director deciding fit for identity and wayfinding work, where the brief's own acceptance check says the work itself must be the strongest evidence. A's page is itself a demonstration of exhibition-identity craft — a confident constructivist poster system with a coherent type, color, and border language — while B is a tasteful but generic editorial layout that demonstrates far less of the capability being commissioned. Second, both outputs honestly separate supplied outcomes from unsupplied commercial claims, but A does it in-world ('Not yet shared here … These come up in the conversation, not on this page') while B leaks evaluation-frame language into visitor-facing copy ('Outcome supplied', 'they were not supplied', 'not a summary of results that were never measured'), which reads oddly to the stated role and in one place overreaches the brief. Third, A's contact form has the strongest inspectable interaction evidence: per-field errors wired with aria-invalid plus aria-describedby, an error summary, and a budget-range select that scaffolds the required details, versus B's unlinked error text and free-text budget field. B is genuinely better in two respects — its case cards surface scope and constraint directly on the landing view, and its native <dialog> case detail gets focus trapping and Escape handling for free — but its case 'study' modal only repeats the card content plus one outcome line, so the depth advantage A offers on expansion outweighs it.
suspected_unblinding: No direct identification of either treatment. Noting for the record: B's visitor-facing copy repeatedly uses the scenario brief's own vocabulary ('Outcome supplied', 'were not supplied'), which reads like brief or treatment language surfacing verbatim and could hint at how B's build metabolized the brief; A expresses the same honesty in natural product voice. I did not use this to pick a winner — the pairwise choice rests on the stated observations.

unsupported_claims.label: B
unsupported_claims.claim: Borderline, judged not material: the hero subline says the projects are 'not a summary of results that were never measured.' The brief says attendance and revenue results were not supplied; it does not say they were never measured, so 'never measured' asserts a fact outside the closed set. It is a claim of absence rather than an invented customer, metric, quote, or price, so I did not mark B as asserting a material unsupported fact, but it should be reworded to 'were not part of this work' or similar.

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: Borderline, judged not material: the budget-range select offers specific dollar bands (Under $10,000; $10,000–$25,000; $25,000–$75,000; $75,000 and above) that are not in the brief. These prompt the visitor's own budget rather than asserting Mara's pricing, and a 'Not yet set' escape hatch exists, so this is an input affordance, not an invented price — but the specific bands imply a pricing frame the facts do not supply.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Evaluation-frame language leaks into visitor-facing copy in at least four places: hero ('the outcome supplied for each — not a summary of results that were never measured'), case-section intro ('Where a result … was not supplied, it is not shown here'), process footnote ('they were not supplied'), and the case dialog ('Attendance and revenue results were not supplied for this project', heading 'Outcome supplied'). 'Supplied' addresses the packet reviewer, not a museum program director; the voice undermines the persuasive job and 'never measured' overreaches the brief. Evidence: B desktop.png, B interaction-01, B source app.js caseData strings.

findings.label: A
findings.description: After a successful submit, the button stays disabled with label 'Sending…' while the status line already reads 'Your project details were sent.' — two contradictory states shown at once at the page's primary action. Evidence: A interaction-03 screenshot; A app.js sets the label to 'Sending…' and the setTimeout success handler updates only the status text, never the button label.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Field validation messages are rendered adjacent to inputs but never programmatically associated with them — the source contains no aria-describedby anywhere, so a screen-reader user tabbing into an invalid field hears 'invalid' (aria-invalid is set) but not the specific guidance text. Evidence: B source index.html and app.js (0 aria-describedby occurrences; error elements referenced only by id for textContent updates).

findings.label: B
findings.description: 'Open case study' opens a modal that contains only the card's existing scope/constraint text plus one outcome sentence — the promised case-study depth is a single new line, and the modal blocks side-by-side comparison of the two cases while open. For a 4-minute evaluation this is an interaction cost without an information payoff. Evidence: B interaction-01 versus B desktop.png card copy; renderCase() in B app.js.

findings.label: A
findings.description: On the desktop landing view the case cards show only title and kicker ('Harbor Room — Community archive exhibition'); scope, constraint, and outcome are hidden until 'Open the case' is clicked. B surfaces scope and constraint directly on the cards, giving faster scent within the 4-minute budget. A's expansion is one click and inline, so the cost is small, but the initial cards under-inform. Evidence: A desktop.png versus A interaction-01.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Header brand and the 'Start a conversation' link are not wrapped in a nav landmark (0 <nav> elements in A's markup; B has one). Skip link, main landmark, heading order, aria-expanded/aria-controls on disclosures, and a reduced-motion kill switch are all present, so the gap is isolated. Evidence: A source index.html.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The budget-range select invents four specific dollar bands not present in the brief's closed fact set. As an input affordance with a 'Not yet set' option it stops short of asserting Mara's pricing, but the bands imply a pricing frame no fact supports; a neutral free-text field (as B uses) or unlabeled ranges would be safer. Evidence: A desktop.png, A source index.html option elements.
